neighbours.label: ' in' (or the word right after it) introducing where a quality or influence shows itself: 'evident in everything', 'seen in', 'reflected in', 'in the way she ...'; locative and temporal 'in' is quiet
fire: His training as an architect is apparent in everything he designs.
The influence of jazz can be heard in many of her later songs.
You can see her confidence in the way she walks into a room.
The city's long history is reflected in its crooked streets and old stone walls.
Their kindness comes through in small acts that nobody else notices.
The author's bitterness is visible in nearly every chapter of the memoir.
The team's exhaustion showed in the way they played the second half.
Traces of the old dialect can still be found in the speech of older villagers.
quiet: His office as an architect is located in a converted warehouse.
The jazz festival will be held in early September.
She left her umbrella in the hallway by the door.
The city's oldest bakery reopened in 2019 after a fire.
They keep the spare blankets in a wooden chest upstairs.
The author was born in a fishing village in Norway.
The team arrived in Madrid two days before the match.
Older villagers still gather in the square every evening.
